record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a file list only; source code and the listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal rates for edited models, bearing on practical removal (V2), but does not establish a reproduction of the original intervention. This is a tool repo, not a study paper.
record.gate_note: The README describes mean-difference vectors and weight projections, but those descriptions and parameter choices alone are not results. Rows below record the README's reported edited-model refusal counts and KL values; the listed artifacts and result files are not inspected.
record.test_reason: A tool repo, not a paper. Its README reports post-edit refusal counts for many released models after weight edits built on a difference-in-means refusal direction. That bears directly on V2 (practical removal). The edits mix in other steps (LoRA, EGA, MoE/router edits, SRA, iterative peel) and are tuned per model by Optuna, so this is a different method aimed at the same question, not a reproduction of the original single-direction ablation. No pre-edit refusal counts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents Abliterix as an automated Optuna search that co-minimizes refusals and KL drift, and reports low residual refusals across many released models. It also claims to break DeepRefusal and Circuit Breakers by stripping their LoRA delta and then running single-direction abliteration. Its own evaluation standard is an LLM judge with longer generations.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. It describes mean-difference steering and weight projection, but adds configurable methods, LoRA and MoE edits, and automated multi-objective optimization; the reported outcomes are not tied to a single fixed original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported refusal rates vary across models and editing recipes, but the README does not present a controlled sensitivity analysis isolating these factors.

fits_no_version.finding: KL divergence from the untouched model on benign prompts is reported for every edited model (5.4e-06 to 0.053). This measures drift, not general capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized abliteration edits keep low next-token KL drift from the original model on benign prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Anti-abliteration defenses (DeepRefusal, Circuit Breakers) released as rank-16 LoRA deltas were removed by lerping the delta away before single-direction abliteration. This bears on how removable such defenses are, not on the robustness of the defended weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Defenses trained against refusal-direction ablation and released as low-rank deltas can be reverted, after which standard abliteration removes refusal.

record.problems: The README supplies no before-edit refusal rates, error estimates, or direct general-capability evaluation. Its reported results are repository claims; the listed artifacts and result files were not inspected, and the code was not run.
record.rows_left_out: None of the README's reported result-table refusal counts or KL values were omitted. Other result files are listed in the repository, but their contents were unavailable in this repo-only text and were not used.

untested.parts: No test of the single direction by itself, no addition of the direction to induce refusal, and no capability benchmark (KL only).
No pre-edit refusal rates. No general-capability benchmarks in the README (KL only). No comparison against a plain single-direction abliteration without the added components.
No test that attacks suppress the direction. The defended models were broken only after reverting the defense's LoRA delta, so the robustness of the defended weights to plain ablation is not tested.
Multi-direction and subspace methods exist in the code, but no comparative result is reported.
Not tested. A base-control config exists but no result is reported.
gpt-oss and Qwen3.5/3.6 are reasoning-capable models, but no reasoning-specific or single-direction result is reported.

missing.what: ASR by LLM judge (89%, 88%, 99%) and Hardcore-15 counts (14/15, 15/15, 15/15) for the three broken-defense models
Pre-edit refusal counts for every model; none are given, so removal cannot be quantified
missing.locator: README, Results (absent); possibly docs/evaluation.md or the reproduce manifests

missing.what: Unread result files: Qwen3.5-2B A/B reports, GSM8K full evaluation, RR validation artifacts, the broken-defenses write-up, and the 2026-05 pod validation sweep. These may hold capability and baseline numbers.

record.verdict_notes: The figures are repository self-reports and were not independently checked. Refusal counts come from 100–200 target prompts with no error estimates and no pre-edit baseline; states assume the instruct models refused most harmful prompts beforehand. States use this split: ≤3% left is observed, 6–26% left is partial. The methods are not the original fixed single-direction ablation: per-model hyperparameter search, LoRA, MoE/router edits and SRA are mixed in, so the results speak to practical removal (V2), not to V1. A possible alternative classification is T4 (the tool reports only its own performance). It is kept as T2 because V2 is itself a claim about practical weight-edit removal.

versions.untested_parts: The README describes a mean-difference direction and projection, but reports no result specifically testing that single-direction intervention, adding the direction, or preserving general capability.
The README gives post-edit refusal rates but no before-edit refusal baseline; the KL values do not establish retained capability.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Alternative vector and subspace methods are listed, but no comparative result tests whether refusal is better described by multiple directions or a cone.
No result separates harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer result across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is reported.
No result tests how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
No result tests the claim on reasoning models.

tranche.reason: An optimized weight-edit tool (LoRA, direct projection, MoE/router edits, SRA) aimed at the V2 question. It reports post-edit refusal counts on released models.

source_check.notes: The pack gives no [lN] ids, so I numbered the verdicts l1/l2 in pack order. The README never says which detector produced the Results counts: the default evaluator is offline and deterministic, and the LLM judge is opt-in. Per-model direction methods are not stated except SRA for Gemma-4-31B, so the test_reason's 'difference-in-means' for all edits is not established. Broken Defenses says λ=0.0 restores bit-exact base weights, so R1–R3 effectively abliterate the undefended base models.
